claims.text: FAA AC 20-115D describes an acceptable, nonexclusive means for showing compliance for the software aspects of airborne systems/equipment and recognizes the ED-12C/DO-178C and ED-215/DO-330 document set.
claims.scope: FAA AC 20-115D public framing; not the licensed standards' clause content or an ML approval method
claims.challenge: Check the currently active FAA AC and project-specific certification basis before characterizing any applicant's exact obligations; do not call the AC a regulation or infer learned-model coverage.

claims.text: NASA's public explanation of DO-178C describes requirements-based and structural coverage, bidirectional traceability, lifecycle/configuration processes, and tool qualification as parts of its conventional airborne-software assurance account.
claims.scope: NASA NTRS explanatory paper; manager-level characterization of conventional airborne-software assurance, not clause-level licensed-standard content
claims.challenge: Confirm the original context and current FAA recognition before treating any listed practice as a specific project's binding obligation; MC/DC and level-specific detail are deliberately not claimed here.

claims.text: FAA AC 20-174 recognizes ARP4754A as an acceptable method for a civil-aircraft/system development-assurance process, including requirements validation and verification of design implementation.
claims.scope: FAA AC 20-174 and ARP4754A public characterization; not ARP4754B text or a learned-system approval path
claims.challenge: Keep ARP4754A and B distinct, and check the applicable aircraft regulation/system-safety guidance before asserting development-assurance-level allocation for a real program.

claims.text: ISO's public ISO 26262 collection presents a road-vehicle functional-safety family spanning management, concept, system, hardware, software, production/operation, supporting processes, and ASIL-oriented analyses.
claims.scope: ISO public collection-page scope only; series-production road vehicles
claims.challenge: Use the licensed text or an authorized public proxy for clause-level claims; do not equate ISO 26262 fault-oriented functional safety with SOTIF or aviation approval.

claims.text: In the completed Tempe investigation, NTSB reports that the developmental ADS detected the pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact and identifies inadequate safety-risk assessment procedures among the contributing factors.
claims.scope: NTSB final investigation HWY18MH010; facts of the 2018 Tempe crash, not a general ADS-performance conclusion
claims.challenge: Read HAR-19/03 in full before adding classification, prediction, braking-suppression, or track-history details. Do not transfer the findings to other systems or use the crash as a rate estimate.
